cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus (1 Corinthians 1:1), is writing to the church in Corinth, and this part is about praying and prophesying. He opens it with a compliment. In WRITING, friend, and all I ever got in the drawer was old takeout menus.

cards.question: What does Paul commend the Corinthians for?

answers.text: Remembering him and keeping his traditions
Sending gifts to help with his travels
Ending all the quarrels among them

cards.text: Then Paul says he wants them to understand something, and he lays out a chain of heads, three links long. I've got one head, friend, and it's mostly hat.

cards.question: In Paul's chain of heads, who is the head of Christ?
In that same chain, Paul says the head of the woman is man, and the head of every man is ___.

cards.text: Now Paul gets specific about covering your head when you pray or prophesy. And I'm standing here in a chef's hat taller than I am, listening VERY closely.

cards.question: What does Paul say a man does when he prays or prophesies with his head covered?
Paul says a woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered honors her head.

cards.text: Paul says that's just as if her head were shaved. Then he follows that thought one step further.

cards.question: If it's shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off, Paul says she should ___ her head.
Paul says a man ought not to cover his head. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He is the image and glory of God
He leads the prayers out loud
He was the first to be baptized

cards.text: And the woman, Paul says, is the glory of man. Then he reaches all the way back to creation, to the very first man and woman.

cards.question: Looking back to creation, Paul says man came from woman.

cards.text: Paul stays at creation for one more line. Man wasn't created for woman, he says, but woman for man.
We're back with Paul, still talking about covering the head in prayer and prophecy. For this reason, he says, a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head.

cards.question: Paul says a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head. Because of whom?

cards.text: Paul doesn't explain the angels part here, and when the text leaves it open, so does Papa. Then Paul turns with a big HOWEVER, to how things are in the Lord.

cards.question: In the Lord, Paul says woman is not independent of man, and man is not independent of woman.
Paul says woman came from man. Then how does he say man comes into the world?

answers.text: He is named by his father
He is raised by the church

cards.question: After all that, Paul says everything comes from ___.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to the Corinthians with a question: is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?

cards.question: Right before Paul asks whether it's proper for a woman to pray with her head uncovered, what does he tell the Corinthians to do?
Paul asks if nature itself teaches that long hair is a disgrace to a man.
For a woman, Paul says long hair is her glory, because it is given to her as a ___.

cards.text: Last, Paul has a word for anyone inclined to dispute all this. Friend, I spent years next to dead batteries that argued all day about who had the most charge left, so I know an argument when I see one coming.

cards.question: What does Paul say to anyone inclined to dispute what he's taught about head coverings?

answers.text: We and the churches of God have no other practice
Each church may choose its own way to do this
Bring it to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem

findings.problem: The first half of 1 Corinthians 11:6 ('If a woman does not cover her head, she should have her hair cut off') is never told or asked. Card 9 only says Paul 'follows that thought one step further,' and card 10 tests only the second half of the verse. The baker misses a step in Paul's argument (uncovered, then cut; cutting is shameful, so cover).

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question asks how man 'comes into the world.' Only the right answer, 'He is born of woman,' describes coming into the world. 'He is named by his father' and 'He is raised by the church' are a different kind of thing, so the question rules them out and the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin refers to himself in the third person ('so does Papa'). The line is also commentary on how he handles the text ('when the text leaves it open, so does Papa') rather than a moment of the passage or a joke.
findings.question: May Papa Dorin refer to himself in the third person as 'Papa,' and may he comment on his own approach of leaving open what the text leaves open, or should story cards only tell the passage and his reactions to it?
